title: My first independent game is finally starting to sell; here’s an update on how things are going so far.
author: PandaRojasStudios
selftext:
After months of developing my first indie game, Nova Survivors, I wanted to share a quick update on how things are going financially.

Here are the current numbers from Steam:

$336 in gross revenue

$283 in net revenue

197 total units (105 Steam purchases + 92 retail activations)

298 wishlists

125 unique users over the game's lifetime

2 hours and 55 minutes median playtime

I know these aren't huge numbers—especially compared to many indie games that have done well—but for my first project, every single sale means something.

The experience has been a massive learning process. I’ve learned so much about development, publishing on Steam, marketing, community building, and just how difficult it is to get people to discover an indie game.

I’d love to hear from other indie developers:

How did sales go for your first game during its initial months?

What marketing strategies actually worked for you?

I’m sharing this because I believe it’s important to show the reality of indie development, not just the success stories.

Thanks for reading!

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4982990/Nova\_Survivors/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4982990/Nova_Survivors/)
